idiom_name: prototype-chain delegation (Object.create / class extends) plus explicit method forwarding
implementation_notes: Delegation is not an add-on in JavaScript but the inheritance mechanism itself: a property lookup that misses on the object continues up the [[Prototype]] chain, so `Object.create(delegate)` gives an object the delegate as its behavioural parent and `class`/`extends` is sugar over the same relation. Two consequences matter for this pattern: `this` inside a forwarded prototype method is the receiving object, so delegate calls do reach the wrapper's own overrides (unlike classic OO delegation), and the prototype can be swapped at run time with `Object.setPrototypeOf`. Where forwarding must also intercept writes, deletes and own-property enumeration, use `Proxy` with `Reflect` - that is interception (the Proxy pattern), not plain delegation.
pitfalls: A method detached from its object (`const save = counting.save`) loses its receiver, so calling it later runs with `this === undefined`; bind it or keep the prototype relation intact.

Own properties shadow the prototype silently: a typo in an assignment creates a shadowing property instead of reaching the delegate, and `Object.create(null)` removes even the Object.prototype safety net.

Mutating a shared prototype changes behaviour for every object delegating to it, and a `Proxy` trap that calls `Reflect` on the same proxy recurses infinitely; proxies also cannot reach the target's private `#fields` without explicit `this`-recovery.
